newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money down on good supply, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money down on good supply, poor demand.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday easy at 2.50-3.25 percent against the opening 3.50-4.00 percent on good funds supply and limited demand, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was between 3.25 percent and 3.50 percent.
Rates were likely to open in the same range on Wednesday in the absence of any fresh market-moving factors, dealers said.
"Liquidity is good and likely to remain so till mid-March," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Rates may harden thereafter."
He said liquidity could tighten in mid-March as companies make tax payments ahead of the financial year-end on March 31.
Easy call rates boosted sentiment in the government securities market, said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"Prices went up at first on buying interest triggered off by low call money rates," he said. "But profit-taking by some market participants restricted the price rise."
Traded volumes on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) rose to 2.94 billion rupees on Tuesday against Monday's 2.62 billion, dealers said.

The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock rose to 100.18 rupees from its last traded 100.05, the 13.70 percent 1999 stock to 103.13 from 103.03, and the 13.67 percent 2007 stock to 100.44 from 100.40 rupees, dealers said.
No trades were reported in certificates of deposits and commercial paper, they said.
